receipts.by: builder lane C (claude subagent), for Vandor's review
receipts.what: Synthetic 3-track MP4s (997 Hz sines at -20/-26/-30 dBFS on both channels, FLAC and Opus) read back at exactly -20.0/-26.0/-30.0 LUFS (tolerance 0.1). demux copy: Opus -> .ogg, AAC -> .m4a, FLAC -> .flac, each decoding bit-identical to the source track; the Ogg ends on the nominal length (288000 samples for 6 s; WebM/MKV keep 648 samples of padding). split_channels gives each channel bit-exact. loudnorm_2pass from pink noise at -48.6 LUFS lands at -14.1 (AAC, TP -3.5) and modulated tones at -14.0 (WAV) after one corrective re-render (loudnorm's own meter read the tones 0.33 LU apart from ebur128).

receipts.by: builder lane C (claude subagent), for Vandor's review
receipts.what: 2026-10-11 17-51-11.mp4 (33 min, one Opus track named by the map: Mix): loudness of the whole track 5.0 s (-41.7 LUFS, LRA 12.3, TP -19.3), demux copy to Ogg 0.25 s (warm cache, 41 MB). Chromium (the desktop app's browser pane) plays every demux output in <audio> and decodeAudioData: Ogg Opus decodes to exactly 288000 samples for 6 s, the 33-min Ogg reports 2028.26 s and seeks to 1000 s in 51 ms, but only from a server that answers HTTP Range requests (python http.server does not: duration Infinity, seeks fail).
receipts.how: audio.loudness / audio.demux on the recording; a Range-serving page with fetch + decodeAudioData

notes: arsenal/media/audio.py: every audio track of a recording. tracks() names each a:N (a stream's own title wins; generic encoder names do not count; else the studio's 6-track OBS map HOUSE_TRACKS). loudness: ebur128 I/LRA/TP per track in one decode. silences: silencedetect on the source clock. demux: one Chromium-playable file per track (Chromium has no audioTracks). split_channels: mono WAV per channel. loudnorm_2pass: measured two-pass loudnorm, read back, re-rendered once on a miss. The ffmpeg that arsenal.media.ff locates is a separate process whose licence depends on the build; the one saved on this machine is configured --enable-gpl --enable-version3, so it is not asserted here.
